model.instance: The unknown matrix is arbitrary real $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$. A public integer $0\le r<d$ defines the adjacent algebraic-rank thresholds to distinguish exactly.

assumptions.description: No spectral gap or positive separation from the low-rank set is assumed.

model.parameter_domain_description: Assume $d\ge1$ and integer $0\le r<d$. No error tolerance band or singular-value lower bound is imposed.
model.description_zh: The quantity $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary, with $d\ge1$ and integer threshold $0\le r<d$.
description_paragraphs: The quantity $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary; assume $d\ge1$ and integer threshold $0\le r<d$.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.
operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The quantity $d,r$ is public and $A$ hidden. Any $v\in\mathbb R^d$ returns exact $Av$; no transpose channel is available.
description_paragraphs: The quantity $d,r$ is public and $A$ hidden. Any $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns exact $Av$; no transpose channel is available.

output.feasibility: The binary labels are low_rank for rank(A) ≤ r and high_rank for rank(A) ≥ r + 1.

proofs.title: Independent Gaussian block queries determine the queried column-space rank almost surely.
proofs.body: Draw a d by (r+1) matrix G with independent standard Gaussian entries and query its columns. For each fixed A, rank(AG)=min{rank(A),r+1} almost surely: after an SVD of A, the relevant Gaussian block has maximal possible rank almost surely. Thus rank(AG)<=r exactly when rank(A)<=r. The test uses r+1 queries and is almost surely correct for every fixed input.
